title: ¿Qué has hecho hoy?
blurbEn: Your first past tense. Two words instead of one — 'he trabajado' — and it covers anything still attached to today.
body:
—¿Qué has hecho hoy, Ana?

—He trabajado toda la mañana en la oficina. Después he comido con Sofía en un restaurante nuevo cerca del centro.

—¿Y por la tarde?

—He estudiado un poco y he escrito dos correos. También he hablado con mi madre por teléfono.

—¿Has terminado el trabajo?

—Todavía no. Pero esta semana he trabajado mucho, y mañana es sábado.

—Yo hoy no he hecho nada especial. He dormido hasta las once y he mirado la televisión.
translationEn:
"What have you done today, Ana?"

"I have worked all morning at the office. Afterwards I ate with Sofía at a new restaurant near the centre."

"And in the afternoon?"

"I studied a little and wrote two emails. I also spoke with my mother on the phone."

"Have you finished the work?"

"Not yet. But this week I have worked a lot, and tomorrow is Saturday."

"I haven't done anything special today. I slept until eleven and watched television."

he.note: The same verb as 'hay', doing a completely different job. Here it is a helper: 'he' plus a participle makes a past.

Todavía.note: 'Todavía no' is the standard answer for something not done yet.

phrases.note: 'hoy' is the giveaway. Time that has not finished yet takes this tense.
Two words: 'he' (the helper) plus 'trabajado' (the participle). The participle never changes.
